rows.question: Please generate a summary of the closing balances at the end of each month for each customer transactions, show the monthly changes and monthly cumulative bank account balances. Ensure that even if a customer has no account activity in a given month, the balance for that month is still included in the output.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH
params AS (
  -- adjusted end_date to a value present in the DB per hint
  SELECT date('2020-01-01') AS start_date, date('2020-02-12') AS end_date
),
-- generate month list from start_date to end_date (one row per month)
months_cte(year, month, month_start, month_end) AS (
  SELECT
    CAST(strftime('%Y', start_date) AS INTEGER),
    CAST(strftime('%m', start_date) AS INTEGER),
    date(start_date, 'start of month'),
    date(start_date, 'start of month', '+1 month', '-1 day')
  FROM params
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    CASE WHEN month = 12 THEN year + 1 ELSE year END,
    CASE WHEN month = 12 THEN 1 ELSE month + 1 END,
    date(month_start, '+1 month'),
    date(month_start, '+2 month', '-1 day')
  FROM months_cte, params
  WHERE month_start < date(params.end_date, 'start of month')
),
customers AS (
  -- include all customers seen in transactions; ensures customers with no activity in some months are included
  SELECT DISTINCT customer_id FROM customer_transactions
),
-- cumulative balance for each customer as of each month_end
cust_month_cume AS (
  SELECT
    c.customer_id,
    m.year,
    m.month,
    m.month_end,
    COALESCE(SUM(t.txn_amount), 0) AS month_end_balance
  FROM customers c
  CROSS JOIN months_cte m
  LEFT JOIN customer_transactions t
    ON t.customer_id = c.customer_id
   AND date(t.txn_date) <= m.month_end
  GROUP BY c.customer_id, m.year, m.month, m.month_end
),
-- get prior month balance to compute monthly change
cust_month_prev AS (
  SELECT
    cmc.customer_id,
    cmc.year,
    cmc.month,
    cmc.month_end,
    (SELECT cm2.month_end_balance
     FROM cust_month_cume cm2
     WHERE cm2.customer_id = cmc.customer_id
       AND (
             (cmc.month = 1 AND cm2.year = cmc.year - 1 AND cm2.month = 12)
          OR (cmc.month > 1  AND cm2.year = cmc.year     AND cm2.month = cmc.month - 1)
       )
     LIMIT 1
    ) AS prior_month_balance
  FROM cust_month_cume cmc
)
SELECT
  cmc.customer_id,
  cmc.year,
  cmc.month,
  cmc.month_end,
  cmc.month_end_balance AS month_end_balance,
  (cmc.month_end_balance - COALESCE(cmp.prior_month_balance, 0)) AS monthly_change,
  cmc.month_end_balance AS cumulative_balance
FROM cust_month_cume cmc
LEFT JOIN cust_month_prev cmp
  ON cmp.customer_id = cmc.customer_id
 AND cmp.year = cmc.year
 AND cmp.month = cmc.month
ORDER BY cmc.customer_id, cmc.year, cmc.month

rows.question: Please help me identify the top 3 bowlers who, in the overs where the maximum runs were conceded in each match, gave up the highest number of runs in a single over across all matches. For each of these bowlers, provide the match in which they conceded these maximum runs.   b.over_id,

  b.bowler,
  SUM(
    COALESCE(bs.runs_scored,0) + COALESCE(er.extra_runs,0)
  ) AS runs_in_over
FROM ball_by_ball b
LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
  ON b.match_id = bs.match_id
  AND b.over_id = bs.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = bs.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = bs.innings_no
LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
  ON b.match_id = er.match_id
  AND b.over_id = er.over_id
  AND b.ball_id = er.ball_id
  AND b.innings_no = er.innings_no
GROUP BY
  b.match_id,
  b.over_id,
  b.team_bowling,
  b.bowler

       m.match_id AS match,
       o.runs_in_over
FROM (
  SELECT b.match_id,
         b.over_id,
         b.innings_no,
         b.bowler,
         SUM(bs.runs_scored) + COALESCE(SUM(er.extra_runs),0) AS runs_in_over
  FROM ball_by_ball b
  LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
    ON bs.match_id = b.match_id AND bs.over_id = b.over_id AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no

  GROUP BY b.match_id, b.over_id, b.innings_no, b.bowler
) o
JOIN (
  SELECT match_id, MAX(runs_in_over) AS match_max
  FROM (
    SELECT b.match_id,
           b.over_id,
           b.innings_no,
           SUM(bs.runs_scored) + COALESCE(SUM(er.extra_runs),0) AS runs_in_over
    FROM ball_by_ball b
    LEFT JOIN batsman_scored bs
      ON bs.match_id = b.match_id AND bs.over_id = b.over_id AND bs.ball_id = b.ball_id AND bs.innings_no = b.innings_no
    LEFT JOIN extra_runs er
      ON er.match_id = b.match_id AND er.over_id = b.over_id AND er.ball_id = b.ball_id AND er.innings_no = b.innings_no
    GROUP BY b.match_id, b.over_id, b.innings_no
  )
  GROUP BY match_id
) mm
  ON o.match_id = mm.match_id AND o.runs_in_over = mm.match_max
JOIN player p ON p.player_id = o.bowler
JOIN match m ON m.match_id = o.match_id

rows.question: Please examine our database records for Chinese cities (country_code_2 = 'cn') during July 2021 and identify both the shortest and longest streaks of consecutive date entries. For each date in these streaks, return exactly one record per date along with the corresponding city name. In your output, please ensure the first letter of each city name is capitalized and the rest are lowercase. Display the dates and city names for both the shortest and longest consecutive date streaks, ordered by date.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH cn_dates AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT city_name, insert_date
  FROM cities
  WHERE country_code_2 = 'cn'
    AND insert_date BETWEEN '2021-04-01' AND '2021-07-21'
),
numbered AS (
  SELECT
    city_name,
    insert_date,
    julianday(insert_date) - ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY city_name ORDER BY insert_date) AS grp
  FROM cn_dates
),
streaks AS (
  SELECT
    city_name,
    MIN(insert_date) AS streak_start,
    MAX(insert_date) AS streak_end,
    CAST(julianday(MAX(insert_date)) - julianday(MIN(insert_date)) + 1 AS INTEGER) AS streak_len
  FROM numbered
  GROUP BY city_name, grp
),
bounds AS (
  SELECT MIN(streak_len) AS min_len, MAX(streak_len) AS max_len
  FROM streaks
),
selected_streaks AS (
  SELECT s.*
  FROM streaks s
  JOIN bounds b ON s.streak_len IN (b.min_len, b.max_len)
)
SELECT
  d.date AS date,
  (UPPER(SUBSTR(c.city_name,1,1)) || LOWER(SUBSTR(c.city_name,2))) AS city_name
FROM selected_streaks s
JOIN legislation_date_dim d
  ON d.date BETWEEN s.streak_start AND s.streak_end
JOIN (
  -- pick one city_name match per streak (city_name already in streaks)
  SELECT DISTINCT city_name, city_name AS city_name_key
  FROM cities
) c ON c.city_name_key = s.city_name
ORDER BY
  CASE WHEN s.streak_len = (SELECT MIN(streak_len) FROM streaks) THEN 1 ELSE 2 END,
  d.date ASC

rows.question: Considering all races where pit stop data is available, and focusing on instances when a driver was not behind another car on the previous lap but is behind on the current lap (accounting for retirements, pit-stop entries, pit-stop exits, and race starts), how many times has each type of overtake occurred in Formula 1?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH races_with_pits AS (
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id FROM pit_stops
),
consecutive_positions AS (
  -- consecutive laps for same driver in races that have pit data
  SELECT
    p_prev.race_id,
    p_prev.driver_id,
    p_prev.lap AS lap_prev,
    p_curr.lap AS lap_curr,
    p_prev.position AS position_prev,
    p_curr.position AS position_curr
  FROM lap_positions p_prev
  JOIN lap_positions p_curr
    ON p_prev.race_id = p_curr.race_id
   AND p_prev.driver_id = p_curr.driver_id
   AND p_curr.lap = p_prev.lap + 1
  JOIN races_with_pits rwp ON rwp.race_id = p_prev.race_id
  WHERE p_prev.position IS NOT NULL
    AND p_curr.position IS NOT NULL
),
pit_flags AS (
  -- mark that a driver pitted on a lap (using pit_stops.lap)
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, lap, 1 AS pitted
  FROM pit_stops
),
retire_flags AS (
  -- mark that a driver retired on a lap (use retirements.lap)
  -- retirements.lap stored as TEXT in schema, so cast to integer where possible
  SELECT DISTINCT race_id, driver_id, CAST(lap AS INTEGER) AS lap, 1 AS retired
  FROM retirements
  WHERE lap IS NOT NULL AND lap <> ''
),
overtake_events AS (
  -- events where driver was NOT behind on previous lap but IS behind on current lap
  SELECT
    cp.race_id,
    cp.driver_id,
    cp.lap_prev,
    cp.lap_curr,
    cp.position_prev,
    cp.position_curr
  FROM consecutive_positions cp
  WHERE
    -- "not behind on previous lap" -> we interpret as position_prev <= position_curr - this query per brief:
    -- more strictly: was not behind (i.e. was ahead or equal) on previous lap but is behind on current lap
    cp.position_prev <= cp.position_curr - 1
    AND cp.position_curr > cp.position_prev
),
overtake_classified AS (
  SELECT
    oe.race_id,
    oe.driver_id,
    oe.lap_prev,
    oe.lap_curr,
    -- determine type with precedence R > P > O
    CASE
      WHEN rf.retired = 1 THEN 'R'
      WHEN pf_curr.pitted = 1 OR pf_prev.pitted = 1 THEN 'P'
      ELSE 'O'
    END AS overtake_type
  FROM overtake_events oe
  LEFT JOIN pit_flags pf_curr
    ON pf_curr.race_id = oe.race_id AND pf_curr.driver_id = oe.driver_id AND pf_curr.lap = oe.lap_curr
  LEFT JOIN pit_flags pf_prev
    ON pf_prev.race_id = oe.race_id AND pf_prev.driver_id = oe.driver_id AND pf_prev.lap = oe.lap_prev
  LEFT JOIN retire_flags rf
    ON rf.race_id = oe.race_id AND rf.driver_id = oe.driver_id AND rf.lap = oe.lap_curr
)
SELECT
  overtake_type,
  COUNT(*) AS overtake_count
FROM overtake_classified
GROUP BY overtake_type
ORDER BY overtake_count DESC

rows.question: What is the average total quantity across all final packaging combinations, considering only the leaf-level items within each combination after fully expanding any nested packaging relationships?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH RECURSIVE
pack_expanded(packaging_id, contains_id, qty) AS (
  -- base: direct relations (if none, no rows for that packaging)
  SELECT packaging_id, contains_id, qty
  FROM packaging_relations
  UNION ALL
  -- recursive: if a contained item is itself a packaging, expand its contents
  SELECT pe.packaging_id,
         pr.contains_id,
         pe.qty * pr.qty
  FROM pack_expanded pe
  JOIN packaging_relations pr
    ON pe.contains_id = pr.packaging_id
),
-- identify leaf items for each root packaging: those contains_id that are not packaging_ids (i.e., not parents in packaging_relations)
leaf_items AS (
  SELECT
    pe.packaging_id,
    pe.contains_id,
    pe.qty
  FROM pack_expanded pe
  LEFT JOIN packaging_relations maybe_child
    ON pe.contains_id = maybe_child.packaging_id
  WHERE maybe_child.packaging_id IS NULL
),
-- also include packagings that have no relations at all: they contain nothing -> total 0
all_packaging AS (
  SELECT id AS packaging_id FROM packaging
),
total_per_packaging AS (
  SELECT
    a.packaging_id,
    COALESCE(SUM(li.qty), 0) AS total_qty_per_packaging
  FROM all_packaging a
  LEFT JOIN leaf_items li
    ON a.packaging_id = li.packaging_id
  GROUP BY a.packaging_id
)
SELECT AVG(total_qty_per_packaging) AS average_total_quantity_across_final_packaging_combinations
FROM total_per_packaging

rows.question: Can you calculate the median from the highest season goals of each team?
rows.pred_sql:
WITH team_season_goals AS (
  -- compute total goals per team per season (counting goals they scored in each match)
  SELECT
    t.team_api_id,
    t.team_long_name,
    m.season,
    SUM(
      CASE
        WHEN m.home_team_api_id = t.team_api_id THEN COALESCE(m.home_team_goal,0)
        WHEN m.away_team_api_id = t.team_api_id THEN COALESCE(m.away_team_goal,0)
        ELSE 0
      END
    ) AS season_goals
  FROM "Team" t
  JOIN "Match" m
    ON t.team_api_id = m.home_team_api_id OR t.team_api_id = m.away_team_api_id
  GROUP BY t.team_api_id, t.team_long_name, m.season
),
team_max_season_goals AS (
  -- highest season goals for each team
  SELECT
    team_api_id,
    team_long_name,
    MAX(season_goals) AS max_season_goals
  FROM team_season_goals
  GROUP BY team_api_id, team_long_name
),
ordered_values AS (
  -- rank the values to help compute median
  SELECT
    max_season_goals AS value,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY max_season_goals) AS rn,
    COUNT(*) OVER () AS cnt
  FROM team_max_season_goals
)
SELECT
  CASE
    WHEN cnt = 0 THEN NULL
    WHEN (cnt % 2) = 1 THEN
      -- odd: middle value
      (SELECT value FROM ordered_values WHERE rn = (cnt+1)/2)
    ELSE
      -- even: average of two middle values
      (
        (SELECT value FROM ordered_values WHERE rn = cnt/2)
        +
        (SELECT value FROM ordered_values WHERE rn = cnt/2 + 1)
      ) / 2.0
  END AS median_highest_season_goals
FROM (SELECT cnt FROM ordered_values LIMIT 1)

rows.question: Could you provide a list of last names for all students who have completed English courses (where completion is defined as having a ClassStatus of 2), along with their quintile ranks based on their individual grades in those courses? The quintile should be determined by calculating how many students have grades greater than or equal to each student's grade, then dividing this ranking by the total number of students who completed English courses. The quintiles should be labeled as "First" (top 20%), "Second" (top 21-40%), "Third" (top 41-60%), "Fourth" (top 61-80%), and "Fifth" (bottom 20%). Please sort the results from highest performing quintile to lowest (First to Fifth).
rows.pred_sql:
WITH completed_english AS (
  SELECT
    ss.StudentID,
    s.StudLastName,
    ss.ClassID,
    ss.Grade
  FROM Student_Schedules ss
  JOIN Students s ON ss.StudentID = s.StudentID
  JOIN Classes c ON ss.ClassID = c.ClassID
  JOIN Subjects subj ON c.SubjectID = subj.SubjectID
  JOIN Categories cat ON subj.CategoryID = cat.CategoryID
  WHERE ss.ClassStatus = 2
    AND cat.CategoryDescription = 'English'
),
tot AS (
  SELECT COUNT(*) AS total_count FROM completed_english
),
ranks AS (
  SELECT
    e1.StudentID,
    e1.ClassID,
    e1.StudLastName,
    e1.Grade,
    (SELECT COUNT(*) FROM completed_english e2 WHERE e2.Grade >= e1.Grade) AS ge_count
  FROM completed_english e1
)
SELECT
  r.StudLastName AS LastName,
  CASE
    WHEN (r.ge_count * 1.0) / t.total_count <= 0.20 THEN 'First'
    WHEN (r.ge_count * 1.0) / t.total_count <= 0.40 THEN 'Second'
    WHEN (r.ge_count * 1.0) / t.total_count <= 0.60 THEN 'Third'
    WHEN (r.ge_count * 1.0) / t.total_count <= 0.80 THEN 'Fourth'
    ELSE 'Fifth'
  END AS Quintile
FROM ranks r
CROSS JOIN tot t
ORDER BY CASE
  WHEN (r.ge_count * 1.0) / t.total_count <= 0.20 THEN 1
  WHEN (r.ge_count * 1.0) / t.total_count <= 0.40 THEN 2
  WHEN (r.ge_count * 1.0) / t.total_count <= 0.60 THEN 3
  WHEN (r.ge_count * 1.0) / t.total_count <= 0.80 THEN 4
  ELSE 5
END

rows.question: Calculate the duration of each track, classify them as short, medium, or long, output the minimum and maximum time for each kind (in minutes) and the total revenue for each category, group by the category.
rows.pred_sql:
WITH chunk_view_0 AS (
SELECT
    t."TrackId",
    t."Name" AS "TrackName",
    t."Milliseconds",
    (t."Milliseconds" / 60000.0) AS "DurationMinutes",
    t."UnitPrice",
    il."InvoiceLineId",
    il."InvoiceId",
    il."Quantity",
    (il."UnitPrice" * il."Quantity") AS "LineRevenue"
FROM "Track" t
JOIN "InvoiceLine" il ON il."TrackId" = t."TrackId"
WHERE t."Milliseconds" IS NOT NULL
  AND il."UnitPrice" IS NOT NULL
  AND il."Quantity" IS NOT NULL
)
SELECT
  category,
  MIN(duration_minutes) AS min_duration_minutes,
  MAX(duration_minutes) AS max_duration_minutes,
  SUM(revenue) AS total_revenue
FROM (
  SELECT
    t.TrackId,
    t.Milliseconds / 60000.0 AS duration_minutes,
    r.revenue,
    CASE
      WHEN t.Milliseconds / 60000.0 >= stats.min_dur
       AND t.Milliseconds / 60000.0 <= (stats.min_dur + stats.avg_dur)/2.0 THEN 'Short'
      WHEN t.Milliseconds / 60000.0 >  (stats.min_dur + stats.avg_dur)/2.0
       AND t.Milliseconds / 60000.0 <= (stats.avg_dur + stats.max_dur)/2.0 THEN 'Medium'
      WHEN t.Milliseconds / 60000.0 >  (stats.avg_dur + stats.max_dur)/2.0
       AND t.Milliseconds / 60000.0 <= stats.max_dur THEN 'Long'
    END AS category
  FROM Track t
  JOIN (
    SELECT TrackId, SUM(UnitPrice * Quantity) AS revenue
    FROM InvoiceLine
    WHERE UnitPrice IS NOT NULL AND Quantity IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY TrackId
  ) r ON r.TrackId = t.TrackId
  CROSS JOIN (
    SELECT
      MIN(t2.Milliseconds / 60000.0) AS min_dur,
      AVG(t2.Milliseconds / 60000.0) AS avg_dur,
      MAX(t2.Milliseconds / 60000.0) AS max_dur
    FROM Track t2
    JOIN (
      SELECT TrackId
      FROM InvoiceLine
      WHERE UnitPrice IS NOT NULL AND Quantity IS NOT NULL
      GROUP BY TrackId
    ) rev2 ON rev2.TrackId = t2.TrackId
    WHERE t2.Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
  ) stats
  WHERE t.Milliseconds IS NOT NULL
    AND r.revenue IS NOT NULL
) categorized
WHERE category IS NOT NULL
GROUP BY category
ORDER BY CASE category WHEN 'Short' THEN 1 WHEN 'Medium' THEN 2 WHEN 'Long' THEN 3 END
